diffs.diff: humidity_percent_RH: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: The DHT11 datasheet (components101 copy) gives the 40-bit frame as "8bit humidity integer data + 8bit decimal data + 8 bit temperature ... + 8bit parity bit" and works the example "Humidity: 0011 0101=35H=53%RH", i.e. 1 count = 1 %RH, offset 0. The model agrees: it uses the built-in sim kind "dht-sensor" (no per-byte measure/responses fields, so the gate's conversion extractor finds 'none'); the simulator returns the slider value directly as %RH via MicroPython's dht.DHT11, which reads the integer byte as %RH, and the example test expects H=67% for a 67 %RH setting and passes. No scale is missing; the difference is an artefact of how the gate reads built-in sensor kinds.

diffs.diff: temperature_C: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Same datasheet worked example: "Temperature:0001 1000=18H=24℃" (Aosong DHT11 sheet: "8bit humidity integer data + 8bit humidity decimal data + 8bit temperature integer data + 8bit temperature decimal data + 8bit check bit"), i.e. 1 count = 1 °C, offset 0. The model's dht-sensor sim kind presents the temperature slider in °C directly through the DHT11 protocol handled by MicroPython's dht.DHT11, and its example test (set 31 -> expects 'T=31C') passes on ESP32 and Pico per check.json. The model has no explicit per-count constant only because the built-in kind encodes it; the conversion it implements is the datasheet's 1 °C per count.
